content: 1. The enzyme CYP3A4 is involved in the metabolism of olaparib. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) taken orally twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 2. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects occur. 3. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Itraconazole and ondansetron both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Itraconazole and osimertinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Itraconazole and oxaliplatin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Itraconazole and ozanimod both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 11. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Itraconazole and panobinostat both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Pantoprazole decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Itraconazole and pazopanib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg orally once daily and monitor closely for QT prolongation. 15. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 16. Itraconazole and pentamidine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Perphenazine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 19. Phenytoin decreases the levels of itraconazole by increasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole and pimavanserin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current pirtobrutinib dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Once the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for five half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the dose taken before initiating the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 22. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and pitolisant both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Itraconazole and ponesimod both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Prochlorperazine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Promazine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Promethazine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Itraconazole and propafenone both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Protriptyline and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Itraconazole and quetiapine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Rabeprazole decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis due to its monacolin K content, which is chemically identical to lovastatin. 33. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of regorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase regorafenib levels and decrease exposure to its active metabolites M-2 and M-5. Regorafenib is not recommended during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 34. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Itraconazole and ribociclib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg twice daily in patients with a platelet count of 100 x 10^9/L or more when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts below 100 x 10^9/L. 40. Itraconazole decreases the effects of Saccharomyces boulardii by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Systemic or oral antifungals may decrease the activity of probiotics. 41. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and salmeterol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and selpercatinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the selumetinib dose taken before initiating the inhibitor. 44. Sevoflurane and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and siponimod both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Sirolimus is not recommended during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 47. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Itraconazole and solifenacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Itraconazole and sorafenib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Itraconazole and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment. When resuming sparsentan, consider dose titration. 53. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Itraconazole and sunitinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Itraconazole increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Itraconazole and tacrolimus both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For daily use, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day. For as-needed use, limit to 10 mg every 72 hours. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 58. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit talazoparib to 0.75 mg/day. After discontinuing P-gp inhibitors for 3-5 half-lives, increase the talazoparib dose to the pre-inhibitor level. 59. Itraconazole increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tamsulosin is not recommended during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 60. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of tazemetostat with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 61. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Tetrabenazine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Thioridazine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 64. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Itraconazole increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg/day when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 66. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 67. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 68. Itraconazole and toremifene both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 69. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., less than 14 days), administer the inhibitor one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next trabectedin infusion. 70. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Trazodone and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Trifluoperazine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 73. Trimipramine and itraconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 74. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 75. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of vandetanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and vandetanib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 76. Itraconazole and vardenafil both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 77. Itraconazole increases the levels of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and vemurafenib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
